info.name: China Parts Reels API
info.description:
# China Parts Reels API

The short-video ("reels") service behind the China Parts **customer** and **seller** apps.
Read the full guide: `docs/frontend-integration.md`.

## Set up in 2 minutes
1. Import this collection **and** one environment file (`local` or `staging`).
2. Select the environment (top right) and fill in: `customerToken`, `sellerToken` (and `adminKey` for the
   operator folder). A token is what China Parts gave the app at sign-in, **without** the word `Bearer`:
   `12|AbCdEf…`.
3. Run the folders **in order** (right-click the collection, *Run collection*). Test scripts store the ids
   they need in collection variables, so each request feeds the next.

## What is added to every request
- `X-Installation-Id`: a UUID v4, generated once and kept in the `installationId` variable. A real app generates it once per install.
- `Accept-Language`: from the `language` variable (`en` or `ar`).
- `Authorization: Bearer …` only on requests that are signed in. **Guest requests carry no Authorization header at all.**

## Variables
| Variable | Where it comes from |
|----------|--------------------|
| `baseUrl`, `customerToken`, `sellerToken`, `adminKey`, `productId`, `language` | You, in the environment |
| `suspendedToken` | Optional: a token of an account out of good standing, for one error example |
| `installationId` | Generated on the first request |
| `customerAccountId`, `sellerAccountId`, `sellerUsername`, `reelId`, `commentId`, `cursor`, `reelStatus`, `hiddenReelId`, `adminCommentId` | Set by the test scripts |
| `otherAccountId`, `otherCommentId` | Set from *List comments* when someone else has commented (for *Block* and *Report a comment*) |

## Things to know
- Every response (except the three reel-link routes) is `{ "success": true, "data": ..., "message": "..." }`
  or `{ "success": false, "error": "SENTINEL", "message": "...", "statusCode": 400 }`.
- **Uploading needs a file:** open *3 · Seller: publish a reel* → *Upload a reel* → Body, and choose a video.
- A reel is **not visible to others until screening finishes** (seconds). Resend *Check the reel* until it says `published`.
- Saved **examples** on each request are real responses from a test run, with ids, hosts and signatures replaced.

item.name: 2 · Identity: who am I
item.description:
The apps never send a username or a password to this service. They send the China Parts session
token they already have, and the service finds (or creates) the matching **reels account**.

The reels account has its **own id**, which is what every response calls `id`. It is *not* the China
Parts customer or seller number: customer 1 and seller 1 are two different people here, with two
different reels ids. Call `GET /api/users/me` right after sign-in and keep that id.

Set `customerToken` and `sellerToken` in the environment (the part after `Bearer `, e.g. `12|abc…`)
before running this folder.

pm.test('Looks like a customer or seller account', function () { pm.expect(['customer', 'seller']).to.include(body.data.accountType); });

request.description:
**Access:** signed-in (customer or seller).

Call it once after sign-in. The first call with a new China Parts account **creates** the reels
account with an automatic handle derived from the name (for example `Sara_K`); later calls just read it.

- `accountType` is `customer` or `seller`: show or hide seller-only features (upload) with it.
- `name` and `avatarUrl` come from China Parts and cannot be edited here.
- `username` (the handle) and `bio` are the only editable parts, see *Update my handle and bio*.
- `locale` is the language this account's push notifications are written in. It follows the
  `Accept-Language` header the app sends.

This request stores your id in the collection variable `customerAccountId`.

request.description:
**Access:** signed-in, in good standing.

The two things a person may change about their reels identity. Send either or both.

| Field | Rule |
|-------|------|
| `username` | 3 to 30 letters (any script, so Arabic works), digits, `_` or `.`. A handle that is already taken, **in any spelling that normalizes the same**, is `409 USERNAME_TAKEN`. |
| `bio` | Up to 150 characters (counted as characters, so Arabic and emoji count fairly). |

Name, picture and standing belong to China Parts and cannot be changed here.

item.name: 3 · Seller: publish a reel
item.description:
Only **sellers** can publish. The whole life of an upload, from the seller app's point of view:

1. `POST /api/reels` returns **immediately** with `status: "pending_moderation"`. Show "Processing".
2. The service screens the video and description in the background (usually seconds, and within a couple
   of minutes for 95% of uploads).
3. The result is **one of**:
   - `published`: it is now in everybody's feeds. (No push is sent for this: re-read the reel or the
     profile to find out.)
   - `rejected`: it broke the content rules. The seller gets a `reelRejected` push, and the reel shows
     as **Removed** on their own profile. Nobody else ever sees it.
   - `hidden`: later, enough reports took it down for review ("Under review").
4. A seller can replace the product links, and delete the reel, at any time.

Run **Upload a reel** first: attach a `video` file in its Body tab (the Runner cannot pick a file for you).
Without a file, set the `reelId` variable to an existing reel id and skip the upload.

request.description:
**Access:** seller, in good standing. `multipart/form-data`.

| Field | Required | Rule |
|-------|----------|------|
| `video` | yes | MP4, MOV or WebM. At most **100 MB** and **60 seconds**. |
| `thumbnail` | no | JPEG or PNG. Generated from the video when omitted. |
| `description` | no | Up to **2200** characters. `#hashtags` and `@handles` are found in it by the server. |
| `productIds` | no | China Parts product ids, **at most 5**, each one the seller's **own active** product. A JSON list (`[101,102]`) or comma separated (`101,102`). |

Limit: **20 uploads per hour** per account (`429 RATE_LIMITED` after that).

The response is the reel with `status: "pending_moderation"`. For its owner the `videoUrl` is a
short-lived private link (15 minutes), so **do not cache it**: re-read the reel when you need it.

- **Hashtags** come back in `hashtags` in the form the seller typed them (`فلتر_زيت`).
- **Mentions** (`@handle` that matches a real account) come back in `mentions`, and each mentioned
  account gets a `reelMention` push once the reel is **published**.
- **Product cards** come back in `products`, already priced.

Fast start: re-encode with the fast-start flag on the device. The server remuxes as a safety net.

This request stores the reel id in `reelId`.

request.description:
**Access:** optional (here, as the owner).

How the seller app finds out what happened. Call it (or the profile request below) until `status`
is no longer `pending_moderation`.

| `status` | What the app shows the owner | Who else can see it |
|----------|------------------------------|---------------------|
| `pending_moderation` | Processing | Nobody (404) |
| `published` | Live | Everybody |
| `rejected` | Removed | Nobody (404) |
| `hidden` | Under review | Nobody (404) |

A non-owner asking for a reel that is not published gets `404 REEL_NOT_FOUND`: it looks exactly
like a reel that never existed.

**Small window to know about:** in the instant after a reel becomes `published`, its files are
being copied to the public store. A `videoUrl` fetched in that instant can 404 for a second or
two. Retry the fetch; do not treat it as an error.

In the Collection Runner this request **repeats itself** (every 2 seconds, up to 30 times) while the
reel is still `pending_moderation`, so the next folders find a published reel.

item.name: 4 · Guest: signed out
item.description:
**A person who is not signed in can watch.** This is the customer app's open door: no sign-in is
needed to watch the feed, open a shared reel, read comments or see a profile.

Rules for guests:
- Send **no `Authorization` header at all**. Never an empty or stale one: an invalid header is a `401`
  even on a route that is open to guests.
- **Always** send `X-Installation-Id` (a UUID v4 generated once per app install). It is how views are
  counted once per installation. This collection adds it for you.
- Everything that changes something (like, comment, save, follow, repost, report...) answers
  `401 AUTH_REQUIRED`: show the sign-in prompt.
- Guests are rate-limited per installation id and per IP (120 requests a minute per installation).

item.name: 10 · Error catalogue
item.description:
Requests that **fail on purpose**, each with a saved example. Every error has the same shape:

```json
{ "success": false, "error": "SENTINEL", "message": "Human text", "statusCode": 403, "details": { } }
```

on some errors. Also worth handling: `429 RATE_LIMITED` (with a `Retry-After` header: wait, then retry),
`INVALID_CURSOR`, and `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (generic message; nothing to show but "try again").

Some of these only fail with the right fixture (a suspended token, an oversized video). They say so,
and their result is not asserted. Read the saved examples.
